messages.subject: Cholesky factor isn't triangular (rstan 2.8)
parts:
Dear All,

I am trying a simple model that uses Cholesky parametrization over regression parameters. I am also applying the recommended "half cauchy" prior for standard deviation.

However, since my upgrade to rstan 2.8, the sampler didn't works :( Over the last version the sampler even after some rejections it goes to the path, but now it doesn't. Looking for the output, I'm seeing that it complains due the fact that the Cholesky factor isn't triangular.

I am attaching a self explained R script with data and model. Any help shall be extremely appreciable.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Cholesky factor isn't triangular (rstan 2.8)
parts:
Where did the error occur? This may be due to changes
in the Eigen library's use of the unfilled part of a matrix.
You could probably fix the problem directly by filling in
the upper triangle of LG with 0 values. We'll look into
it if you can verify where you're getting the error.

But this is probably all irrelevant for the problem at hand.
You shouldn't need to Cholesky decompose a diagonal matrix
and go through the elaborate multiplication of X with blups.

SG <- diag_matrix(rep_vector(s2g, G));
LG <- cholesky_decompose(SG);
blups <- LG * blupsStd;

I'm pretty sure this reduces to just this:

blups <- diag_matrix(rep_vector(sqrt(s2g) * blupsStd, G));

And then you can further simplify be eliminating
X * blups in favor of just:

yHat <- mu + X * sqrt(s2g) * blupsStd;

At least I think I got the algebra right.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Cholesky factor isn't triangular (rstan 2.8)
parts:
Dear Bob,

Thank you indeed regarding your reply. How can I manually fill the upper values with 0s?

I am getting an error when calling the sampling() statement.

The model is parsed to C++ pretty good as well as compiling with the provided flags.

However when I call to sampling() I get:

SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'ModelCode' NOW (CHAIN 1).
[1] "Error : "                                                                                                                            
[2] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                      
[3] "validate transformed params: LG is not lower triangular; LG[1,2]=6.95128e-310"                                                       
[4] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
[5] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."                            
[6] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                            
[7] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."                                                                        
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

Regarding your suggestions over the code, I can't understand... let me be more clear:

I am trying to avoid sampling the blups (G coefficients) from a MVN, thus I am employing the cholesky trick (documented over the regression chapter of the manual).

They are unknown, as well as their variance. Thus I am sampling their variance using a half-cauchy and blupsStd using a standard normal; after these algebras to build the Sigma I shall get proper scale blups.

I am not sure how is parametrized the Sigma (Variance-Cov Matrices), with variances or standard deviations, specially after your comments!

Keep in touch. Thank you indeed.

Cheers,
FH

> On Oct 12, 2015, at 4:31 PM, FHRB Toledo <fernand...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear Bob,
>
> Thank you indeed regarding your reply. How can I manually fill the upper values with 0s?

{
real zero;
zero <- 0;
for (m in 1:K)
for (n in (m + 1):K)
x[m,n] <- zero;
}

The use of a local variable zero is to avoid creating multiple autodiff
variables. It's not necessary, but helps with efficiency.

As to the rest of your code, I think there's a lot of needless linear
algebra --- in fact, given the diagonal assumptions you're making, it
looks like you can remove Cholesky factors altogether.

- Bob
